components.description: Federal (Title II) family and medical leave: 12 administrative workweeks of unpaid, job-protected leave in a 12-month period for the birth and care of a child, placement for adoption or foster care, care of a spouse with a serious health condition, or the employee's own serious health condition (incl. pregnancy and recovery from childbirth). Employee may substitute own annual or sick leave.
components.faculty_group_note: All civilian members of the faculty (FHB 7.2: civil service leave administration applies to all civilian members of the faculty; Pink Book 11: leave on the same basis as employees in the competitive civil service)
components.eligible_parent_wording: birth of a son or daughter of the employee and the care of such son or daughter; each parent; placement of a son or daughter with the employee for adoption or foster care; care of spouse; own serious health condition
components.entitlement_note: Statutory entitlement (5 U.S.C. 6382(a)(1): an employee shall be entitled); employee must invoke it and give notice.
components.duration_note: 5 U.S.C. 6382(a)(1) and 5 CFR 630.1203(a): "a total of 12 administrative workweeks" (no qualifying word, R13); the HR page and OPM handbook summarise it as "up to 12 workweeks". Birth/placement leave must be concluded within 12 months of the birth or placement; intermittent or reduced-schedule leave for birth/bonding requires the agreement of employee and agency (flagged). Own accrued, accumulated or advanced annual/sick leave or donated leave may be substituted at the employee's election (sick and donated leave for medical purposes such as recovery from childbirth; annual leave for any period); the agency may not require substitution. Military caregiver leave (26 workweeks, 6382(a)(3)) not relevant to a birth.
components.service_requirement: 12 months of service as a covered Federal employee (not required to be consecutive); excludes temporary appointments of 1 year or less and intermittent employees
components.time_window: leave for birth or placement must be concluded within the 12-month period beginning on the date of birth or placement
components.notice: not less than 30 calendar days before leave begins when foreseeable based on an expected birth or placement; otherwise as soon as practicable
components.medical_certification_note: agency may require medical certification for leave for a serious health condition of the employee or of a spouse/son/daughter/parent; leave for birth or placement may require administratively acceptable evidence
components.relief_note: Formal leave without pay; relief not stated (R9).

notes: What the sources contain: the NPS HR Absence & Leave page (FMLA summary, VLTP) and 2017 HRO leave-program slides (annual, sick, FMLA, LWOP, VLTP, advanced leave); the 2016 Faculty Handbook (governing faculty policy by authority of the President; tenure-clock modification 5.1.8; civil service leave administration applies to all civilian faculty, 7.2; quarter system 9.1); the 2015 Pink Book (faculty entitled to leave on the same basis as competitive civil service, 11; special LWOP and sabbatical, 13-14); 5 CFR part 630 (2018 edition) and 5 U.S.C. chapter 63 (2017 edition), which govern leave for NPS civilian faculty; the OPM 2015 handbook on leave for childbirth, adoption and foster care (guidance); DoDI 1400.25-V630 (DoD leave procedures, nothing parental).

missing is false: the Faculty Handbook is a governing faculty handbook (incl. a tenure-clock policy), and 5 U.S.C. chapter 63 and 5 CFR part 630 are the leave law and regulation that FHB 7.2 and Pink Book 6 and 11 apply to the faculty (the rule for records with no governing document, reader instructions §3).

Finding: in 2018 NPS tenure-stream faculty, as federal civilian employees, had no paid parental leave and no employer childbirth benefit; paid time for a birth came only from their own sick and annual leave (incl. advanced leave, repaid) or donated leave. Protected leave is FMLA Title II, 12 administrative workweeks (c1).

Birth parent chain: own sick leave for prenatal care, incapacity and recovery from childbirth (c2; advanced sick leave c4 and donated leave c7 when balances run out) -> annual/advanced annual leave (c5, c6) for bonding; FMLA 12 administrative workweeks (c1) may run with these as substituted paid leave or after sick leave (separate entitlements; OPM: "She can use 6-8 weeks of sick leave for recovery from childbirth, then later invoke FMLA"); discretionary LWOP (c8) after. No sequence links are coded: the documents fix no order between the own-balance components and FMLA, the own-balance components add no paid weeks (R1, R1d) and no protected weeks (U6), and c5, c6, c8 are general-purpose (U1); protected weeks rest on c1 alone.

Non-birth parent chain: own sick leave to care for the birth mother during recovery (c3, up to 12 weeks per leave year; advanced sick leave c4 and donated leave c7 possible) -> annual/advanced annual leave for bonding (c5, c6); FMLA 12 administrative workweeks (c1) for care of a spouse with a serious health condition and/or birth and care of the child, within 12 months; discretionary LWOP (c8). Same reasoning: no sequence links.

Not coded as components: Voluntary Leave Bank (optional agency program; no saved document shows NPS or DON operates one); telework, alternative work schedules, credit hours and compensatory time off (OPM handbook sections H-J; work-schedule flexibilities, not leave or relief); special LWOP for study, research or service (Pink Book 13) and sabbatical (Pink Book 14, FHB 10.5), which cannot be used for a birth; excused absence and administrative leave (DoDI 1400.25-V630, 5 U.S.C. 6329a).

The January 15, 2015 Presidential memorandum (printed as a note to 5 U.S.C. chapter 63 and summarised in the OPM handbook) directs agencies to offer 240 hours of advanced sick leave and the maximum advanced annual leave on request, but states that it creates no enforceable right; advanced leave (c4, c6) is therefore coded discretionary under 5 CFR 630.402 and 5 U.S.C. 6302(d).

Federal FMLA eligibility needs 12 months of federal service, not 1,250 hours; tenure-track appointments (three-year initial terms) are not temporary appointments of 1 year or less, so the two-year member qualifies (U8).

Documents cited but not saved: OPM fact sheets (FMLA; Sick Leave (General Information); Sick Leave for Personal Medical Needs; Sick Leave for Family Care and Bereavement; Sick Leave to Care for a Family Member with a Serious Health Condition; Advanced Sick Leave; Advanced Annual Leave; Voluntary Leave Transfer Program; Voluntary Leave Bank Program; Leave Without Pay; Effect of Extended LWOP; Part-time and Job Sharing; Credit Hours; Definitions Related to Family Member); OPM CPM 2013-14 and CPM 2010-15; OPM memorandum of October 21, 2013; NPS Request for Advance Leave form and routing/approval process; SF 71; OPM630/OPM630A forms; Application to Restore Annual Leave; agency (NPS/DON) internal leave policies and any collective bargaining agreement; 29 CFR part 825; NPSINST 12630.5 (sabbaticals); annual Provost Promotion and Tenure Procedures and Documentation Guidelines; Faculty Bylaws; Faculty Orientation Manual; NPSINST 5330.1 (telework); SECNAVINST 1524.2C; OPNAVINST 5450.210D; DoDI 1402.06; SECNAVINST 12534.1C; NAVPGSCOLINST 12430.2F; DoDI 1215.6.
Calendar: FHB 9.1 states a quarter system with terms of about twelve weeks; recorded as term_weeks 12. No component is measured in terms.
